newsitem.title: JAPAN: Ark Securities eyes trade in unregistered shares.
newsitem.headline: Ark Securities eyes trade in unregistered shares.

text.p: Ark Securities Corp, a small brokerage, says it is gearing up to start broking in unregistered shares as early as this autumn, after regulations prohibiting such activities are lifted.
Japan will finalise procedures next month to implement reforms that include liberalising trade in unlisted shares.

Once approval is given, Ark Securities plans to start by broking about one billion yen worth of shares in 20 firms within the current business year, which ends March 1998, Ark president Tatsuhiko Ando told Reuters in a recent interview.
By end-March 2000, Ark is aiming at broking four billion yen worth of shares in 100 companies, Ando said, rising to 20 billion yen worth of stocks from a few hundred firms the following year.
Business would focus on private investors, with prices set between 50 and 200 yen per share, Ando said.
"Broking in unregistered shares will provide venture businesses with new fund-raising possibilities and private investors will have a new area to invest in," Ando said.
The unlisted firms Ark Securities plans to start broking would have annual sales between 100 million and two billion yen, Ando said.
"In the United States, Nasdaq trades shares of about 5,200 firms and those, together with the pink sheet and local markets, add up to trade in about 23,000 firms," Ando said.
"In Japan there are about 800 firms with shares registered for over-the-counter trade and there is great potential for trade in unregistered shares," he said.
